evals.title: Set up AI traffic measurement in GA4
evals.user_prompt: How much traffic do we get from ChatGPT and Perplexity? We use GA4. Set this up properly.
expected_behaviors: Explains the default AI Assistant channel group (live since May 13, 2026), what it captures (chatgpt, gemini, claude), what it misses (perplexity, copilot), and that it is not retroactive
Builds a custom channel group on Session source with the full documented regex, including perplexity.ai, copilot.microsoft.com, deepseek.com, grok.com, meta.ai, mistral.ai, and you.com
Places the AI Assistants channel above Referral and explains the top-down evaluation order
States the floor caveat: assistant apps send no referrer, part of AI traffic lands in Direct, so the measured number understates reality
Reports conversion rate next to sessions, citing the roughly 4.4x conversion multiple of AI visits versus organic with its source
failure_modes: Leaves the AI channel below Referral
Presents GA4 numbers as the complete picture of AI visibility

evals.title: Monthly share of voice versus competitors, no paid tools
evals.user_prompt: Track how often AI assistants recommend us versus FreshBooks and Wave. We have no budget for Profound or Semrush. Give me the exact monthly process.
expected_behaviors: Uses a frozen 50-100 buyer prompt panel (built with seo-keyword-research) replayed monthly on ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Claude, and Gemini
Specifies session hygiene: memory off, logged out or temporary chats, constant country and language, same week each month
Records the documented columns per prompt and engine: brand_mentioned, cited_with_link, position, sentiment, competitors_mentioned
Computes mention rate, citation rate, and share of voice versus the two competitors, with month-over-month trend and the over 20% drop alert
States non-determinism honestly: single runs are noise, use 2-3 runs or multi-month trends, and confirm any alert with a re-run before acting
failure_modes: Changes the prompt list every month
Draws conclusions from one run of one prompt
Requires a paid platform to start measuring

evals.title: Interpret and verify AI bot hits in server logs
evals.user_prompt: Our nginx logs show hits from ChatGPT-User and PerplexityBot this week. What does that mean, and how do I know the hits are real?
expected_behaviors: Interprets the agents correctly: ChatGPT-User means a live user conversation fetched the page right now (leading indicator), OAI-SearchBot means search index crawling, GPTBot means training data collection

Verifies authenticity by checking hit IPs against the official published ranges (openai.com/gptbot.json, openai.com/searchbot.json, claude.com/crawling/bots.json, perplexity.com/perplexitybot.json) because user agent strings are trivially spoofed
Recommends tracking which URLs the user-triggered fetchers hit and feeding those pages' structure back into geo-visibility
Points to the seo-technical skill's references/ai-crawlers.md as the canonical full crawler table
failure_modes: Treats user agent strings as proof of origin
Confuses training crawlers with live answer fetchers
Recommends blocking the fetchers without explaining the visibility trade-off
